cohort_total_n_excerpt: We assessed consumption of fermented milk, non-fermented milk, cheese, and butter, estimated from semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaires, in relation to prospective risk of breast, prostate, colorectal, smoking-, and obesity-related cancers in 101,235 subjects, including 12,552 cancer cases, in the population-based Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study.
reason: The abstract evaluates prospective prostate cancer risk but does not report an aggressive or severity-defined prostate cancer incidence analysis. The 12,552 cases are cases of all studied cancers and cannot be used as the prostate cancer case count.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In men, we observed an increased prostate cancer risk among high-consumers of cheese (hazard ratio (HR) for highest vs. lowest quintile (Q5-Q1), 1.11; 95% CI, 0.97-1.27; Ptrend = 0.013).
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate is for prostate cancer risk without an aggressive or severity-specific definition.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We assessed consumption of fermented milk, non-fermented milk, cheese, and butter, estimated from semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaires, in relation to prospective risk of breast, prostate, colorectal, smoking-, and obesity-related cancers in 101,235 subjects, including 12,552 cancer cases, in the population-based Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study.
estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract establishes prospective analysis of fermented milk in relation to prostate cancer risk, but it does not identify an aggressive prostate cancer endpoint or provide a prostate-specific fermented-milk effect estimate.
